title: Alien Breed Lua remaster now with all four 2D titles
author: Designer-Camp1815
selftext:
My remaster of the Alien Breed 2 games now supports all four titles. You can play with a reasonably close emulation of the original or enable a bunch of modern features and graphics. Classic graphics only for Tower Assault, modern requires light placement on 50+ levels.

There is a new easy difficulty for Alien Breed 2 that reduces the amount of aliens and makes the first level more forgiving. Tower Assault gets a facility map to make it a bit easier to tell how the levels connect together. Restart Level rewinds back to your level start conditions so you can make another attempt without losing the whole game.

* Twin stick controls with gamepad support or classic directional controls.

Multiplayer:

* Online multiplayer with rollback netcode for two players with UPNP port request.
* Two-player viewport with multiple camera modes including dynamic split screen or full size views.
* More options to share beyond just credits.

Modern mode provides:

* 640×360 virtual canvas scaled by an exact integer to the display (×2 at 720p, ×3 at 1080p = 1920×1080, ×4 at 1440p, ×6 at 2160p). Pixel-perfect, square pixels throughout. 2.8× more world area than classic's 320×256
* Fog of war to let you restrict your viewable area to approximately the original games area.
* Audio system emulates the original four channel behavior via rules while allowing additional channels to play to avoid cut offs. Stereo emulation and distance based falloff for sounds are also simulated.
* Lightweight deferred-lighting mode. Flashlight with real polygon shadow-casting occlusion (not a fake cone) and wall-spill lighting. Static light fixtures are real dynamic lights (falloff, shadows), not painted-on brightness. Props (barrels, etc.) cast their own projected shadows.
* Modern alien pathfinding AI if you want them to be much more aggressive.

Classic mode provides:

* Authentic 320×256 viewport, pixel-aspect-corrected by 16/15 (the real PAL Amiga ratio) so it displays 4:3 pillarboxed 1440×1080 at 1080p. The non square pixel ratio is critical to not requiring letterboxing at modern resolutions, a strange coincidence.
* The original's flat, unlit renderer (no flashlight/shadows at all).
* Original HUD but full speed updates instead of being restricted to one column at a time.
* Accurate 4-channel Paula-style audio, including the original's channel-stealing behavior.
* Original pathfinding.
